newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar drifts back to end softer.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar drifts back to end softer.

text.p: LIFFE white sugar futures slipped back during late Monday trading, with key front month contracts ending a choppy day softer.
Traders said price movements were largely influenced by technical factors and spread business considerations with little in the way of physical stimulus.
March ended the day at $305.10 a tonne, down $0.10 from Friday, having eased from highs of $306.80. LIFFE turnover was 2,607 lots.

Technically, the market is oversold and some chartsists said that although a bounce from the lows is not out of the question, recent movements suggest prices could continue to consolidate before easing further.
In physicals, this week sees the deadline for bids in Syria's tender to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws for Nov/Dec shipment.

Elsewhere, an official in Poland said the country could export some 400,000 tonnes of sugar without subsidies next year as its beet campaign is likely to result in record sugar output of 2.1 million tonnes this year.
